summary: Private deploy: intermittent artifact integrity failures when egress proxy rewrites TLS SNI and splits range requests
description:
Issue summary:
Customers on a private deployment report intermittent artifact integrity check failures during model shard downloads. The serving node logs show successful HTTP range 206 responses but later hash checks fail and streaming sessions reset with TLS errors. Impact: at peak, ~8% of shard fetches for gptx-13b-quant-v1 in us-east fail, causing retries, increased latency, and transient request errors for end users.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC peered to Redwood control plane)
- Customer egress via corporate forward proxy that performs TLS interception for inspection and also acts as an HTTP range coalescing/splitting device.
- Redwood artifact storage: presigned S3 URLs fetched over HTTPS via customer egress.

Steps to reproduce (observed by customer):
1) Start several concurrent generation requests against pinned gptx-13b-quant-v1 on dedicated serving nodes.
2) Watch serving logs: artifact-fetcher requests presigned range downloads for shard parts (range headers present).
3) Intermittently one of the range responses is returned as 206 but the returned payload length is shorter than the byte-range requested (proxy split/trim behavior).
4) Artifact integrity check fails (hash mismatch) and the serving node logs: "artifact validation error: invalid shard hash".
5) Serving runtime retries, attempts full-range re-download, which sometimes succeeds after fallback to a different presigned URL, but adds 300–1200ms latency per request.

Observed runtime logs (sanitized):
- artifact-fetcher: "GET https://s3-presigned... Range: bytes=1048576-2097151 -> 206 Partial Content, content-length: 1048576"
- net/transport: "read: unexpected EOF after 842312 bytes"
- artifact-checker: "validation failed: expected sha256=... got sha256=..."
- tls: "client handshake aborted: tls: unexpected message"

Hypothesis: The customer's forward proxy is performing two problematic behaviors in combination: (1) rewriting TLS SNI for outbound connections to a local inspection name which causes the presigned URL hostname to receive a certificate chain that does not match the original S3 name (benign for some clients but can break HTTP/2 connection pooling and lead to connection reuse anomalies); and (2) the proxy splits/coalesces Range requests (to optimize caching) and occasionally truncates returned ranges or closes TCP connections mid-response during aggressive keepalive recycling. When a partial response is truncated but the proxy still returns 206 with an incorrect content-length, the artifact-checker receives fewer bytes than expected and flags integrity errors. The TLS rewrite can exacerbate connection reuse causing the client to see truncated TLS records or handshake errors on resume, leading to more unsuccessful replays.

Temporary workaround attempted by customer:
- Bypass egress proxy for S3 hosts (route via direct internet egress) — this eliminated failures in their environment (confirms proxy involvement).
- Increase artifact-fetcher retry to more attempts — reduced impact but not acceptable long-term due to increased latency and cost.

Impact to customer: Production traffic experiences increased latency and occasional 5xx errors when shard integrity fails; customer has paused a subset of high-throughput workloads.

Requested from customer: capture tcpdump of failing fetch (pcap) and proxy debug logs showing range-splitting behavior, and confirm whether proxy rewrites SNI for S3 hostnames.

Recommended internal next steps: see investigation_notes.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial ticket from FinSecure Labs. They attached sample artifact-checker logs and a screenshot of the serving node stacktrace. They report ~8% failure rate during peak batch jobs.
2026-03-10 10:04 - Noah Chen: Acknowledged. Asked for pcaps, proxy vendor+version, and whether bypassing the proxy removes the issue. Asked customer to provide control-plane request IDs that failed.
2026-03-10 11:30 - FinSecure Labs (support@finsecure.example): Provided pcap and proxy vendor: 'PerimeterInspect v3.7'. Confirmed bypassing proxy for s3.amazonaws.com stops failures.

2026-03-11 08:26 - Noah Chen (SRE): Initial analysis: observed repeated FIN mid-stream and mismatched content-lengths in pcap. Suspect proxy range-splitting and early close. Added hypothesis about TLS SNI rewrite breaking connection pooling.

2026-03-11 12:15 - Marcus Hale (Networking): Reproduced pattern in lab by deploying PerimeterInspect with range coalescing enabled. Observed same truncated responses when range-splitting and TLS rewrite both enabled. Filed repro notes to GH (related_pr above).

2026-03-12 09:03 - Aisha Kapoor: Sent recommended workaround to customer: configure proxy bypass for s3 presigned domains and disable range-splitting for presigned URL patterns. Asked customer to confirm vendor support ticket opened.

2026-03-12 16:40 - FinSecure Labs: Confirmed vendor opened ticket and will disable range-splitting for presigned URLs as interim fix. Asking Redwood for guidance to detect and surface these failures in Console automatically.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-11 07:50 - Captured pcap analysis: multiple GETs with Range header followed by 206 responses where actual TCP payload length < advertised Content-Length. Several TLS sessions show handshake resumed after server send close, producing 'unexpected EOF' in client read.

2026-03-11 08:12 - Compared working vs failing flows: when proxy bypassed, content-lengths match and no truncated reads. When proxy active, some ranges are returned in multiple TCP segments with final segment missing and FIN injected by proxy.

2026-03-11 10:00 - Kernel/TCP analysis: no retransmissions from origin; truncation occurs at proxy which likely re-maps ranges to cached objects and fails to assemble full body when caching window hits eviction during concurrent fetches.

2026-03-11 11:30 - TLS SNI rewrite check: proxy changes SNI to internal hostname 'inspect.local' resulting in cert name mismatch for s3.amazonaws.com. Client TLS config in artifact-fetcher ignores hostname mismatch for direct S3 but HTTP/2 connection pooling fails leading to reused connections with partial states.

2026-03-11 13:45 - Repro in lab: Enabled range-splitting + sni-rewrite in PerimeterInspect. Observed same artifact hash mismatches and increased 'tls: unexpected message' errors in client, matching customer logs.
2026-03-11 15:00 - Correlation: failing shard parts are biased to high-concurrency ranges and larger byte ranges (>=1MB). Likely related to proxy cache windowing and connection recycling heuristics.
2026-03-12 09:00 - Short-term mitigation validated: bypassing proxy for presigned S3 domains eliminated failures in customer environment.

2026-03-12 11:20 - Long-term options: (a) detect truncated range responses in artifact-fetcher and automatically retry full-range or re-request presigned URL; (b) add explicit Host header validation and verify TLS cert commonName before accepting pooled connection; (c) surface a console alert when a threshold of artifact validation failures occur per deployment to guide customers toward proxy bypass.
2026-03-12 12:30 - Open action: engineering to propose runtime changes to be resilient to proxy range-splitting (see linked PR for initial code sketch).
resolution: Workaround accepted by customer: disable range-splitting/cache-coalescing for presigned S3 URL patterns or configure egress bypass for s3.amazonaws.com. Engineering will implement improved detection and a safer retry strategy: on content-length mismatch or unexpected EOF, artifact-fetcher will attempt a full-range re-download from a fresh connection before failing integrity. Planned rollout: patch to artifact-fetcher in platform v1.78.0 and console alert to surface artifact-integrity spikes. Target ETA for patch: 2026-03-26. Customer will keep workaround until vendor patch is applied.
notes: This ticket documents an intersection of application-layer proxy behavior and TLS interception causing artifact-integrity failures. Related to prior tickets about range/rewrite issues but unique due to combined SNI rewrite + range-splitting behavior. Consider adding guidance to private-deploy runbook about exempting presigned URLs from range-munging proxies.
